$comment: The repository contract. One entry per repository type; a repository is
assigned exactly one type and inherits its required-artifact list plus its
exemptions. Every exemption carries a reason, because an exemption without a
reason is indistinguishable from an oversight, and a contract that cannot say
'why is this allowed here' stops being enforced and starts being negotiable.

language_policy.note: README is the public front page on github.com and the reference repo's is English. Long-form docs/ stay in Russian. No placeholder text may reach a rendered document: every value is read from the repository.

telegram-bot.description: A deployable Telegram bot: Dockerfile, compose, deploy/ and a CI that ships it.

library.description: An importable Python library. It is not a service, so a container image would be a fake artifact.

exemptions.Dockerfile: A library is installed with `pip`/`uv`, not run. An image with no entrypoint would be decorative.

observability-stack.description: A compose-only observability stack. There is no application image; the stack is composed of vendor images.

exemptions.Dockerfile: Every component is a vendor image (Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, Alertmanager, OTel Collector). Nothing in this repository is built.

observability-stack.notes: SECURITY.md is grown from the existing SECURITY-BASELINE.md rather than written from scratch - that file already holds the hardening inventory and must not be lost.

test-tooling.description: A QA harness that runs other projects' bots. It is a library plus a runner, not a service.

exemptions.Dockerfile: The harness imports the bot under test in-process.
exemptions..github/dependabot.yml: Absent today. Recorded as a known gap in the README Status block rather than papered over.
exemptions..env.example: The harness reads no environment variables: Redis is addressed by port on the command line, and there is no secret to template. An .env.example with nothing in it would be a file that teaches the wrong thing.

template.description: A project template. The README documents the project it generates, and CI must validate the generated output.

exemptions.Dockerfile: Lives in the template body, not at the template root.

library-published.description: The format reference. Audited against the contract, not rewritten to it.

exemptions.Dockerfile: An npm library is not containerised.
exemptions..github/CODEOWNERS: Meaningless while there is one owner. Revisit when a second appears.

docs.description: A documentation-only repository. No build, no runtime, therefore no CI.

$comment: Per-repository exceptions to the global policy. Each one records what is
waived and why. An override with no reason is a contract that has stopped

reason: This repository is a methodology document written in Russian by its author,
and the body is 400 lines of substantive prose, not boilerplate. An English
front page here would mean either a full translation -- a large, unreviewed
rewrite of the owner's own writing -- or a thin English shell around a
Russian document that misrepresents itself as the real thing.
The chosen answer: the Russian body is kept intact and an English summary
block is added at the top so the GitHub front page is legible to an English
reader, with a line stating plainly which language the rest is in.
Revisit when the document is next substantively revised by its author.
